subject: Science & Technology
theme: Leadership and institutional history: ISRO chairmen during key satellite missions
question_short_text: ISRO Chairman when INSAT-3B was launched in March 2000
text: Who amongst the following was the Chairman of ISRO when INSAT-3B was launched?
explanation: INSAT-3B was launched on March 22, 2000. Dr. K. Kasturirangan served as the Chairman of ISRO from 1994 to 2003, making him the ISRO chief during this launch.

research.summary: This question tests recall of institutional leadership timelines in ISRO history. Dr. K. Kasturirangan headed ISRO for nine years (1994–2003), a transformative period when the organisation shifted from experimental missions to operational systems. INSAT-3B, launched on March 22, 2000, was the first satellite in the advanced INSAT-3 series, built on the I-2000 satellite bus and intended primarily for business communication and mobile satellite services. Under Kasturirangan's leadership, ISRO achieved major milestones: operationalizing the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) for routine polar orbit missions, conducting the first successful flight test of the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV), developing the second-generation and initiating third-generation INSAT satellites (INSAT-3 series), and launching remote sensing satellites IRS-1C and IRS-1D. The trap in this question lies in the other options: Anil Kakodkar succeeded Kasturirangan in 2003 and headed ISRO until 2009; Abdul Kalam was never ISRO chairman but was closely associated with India's missile programs as Scientific Advisor; U. R. Rao was the first chairman of ISRO (1963–1966) and thus much earlier. Recognizing Kasturirangan's tenure (1994–2003) as encompassing the year 2000 is the quickest solve path.
facts: INSAT-3B was the first satellite in the INSAT-3 series, carrying 12 extended C-band, 3 Ku-band, and CxS mobile satellite service transponders.
Under Kasturirangan's tenure, ISRO transitioned from experimental satellite missions to operational systems in telecommunications, broadcasting, meteorology, and earth observation.
The PSLV was successfully operationalized during Kasturirangan's leadership, enabling routine deployments to sun-synchronous polar orbits starting in 1994.
K. Kasturirangan served as the fifth Chairman of ISRO and also held the position of Secretary to the Department of Space.
INSAT-3B was collocated with INSAT-2E at 83 degrees East longitude in geostationary orbit, enabling optimized use of orbital slots and frequency spectrum.
